To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the law of a component of a solution to a one‐dimensional fully coupled FBSDE is Gaussian; (2) the variance of this component can be bounded by a deterministic function of the initial condition and the terminal condition; and (3) this variance is bounded away from zero.

the law of the solution to an FBSDE with a Lipschitz generator is absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure and that the density of each component of this solution is bounded by a Gaussian density.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the asymptotic behavior of a stochastic process which solves a forward-backward stochastic differential equation (FBSDE) with a Lipschitz continuous generator, and a non-degenerate diffusion coefficient.
the development of a new method for obtaining Gaussian density estimates for solutions to FBSDEs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the main result is the first result of this type in the case where the forward and backward equations have a different degree of nonlinearity.
our approach provides a simple and elegant way to obtain Gaussian density estimates for solutions to FBSDEs.
the Gaussian density estimates for fully coupled FBSDEs are a direct consequence of classical results on parabolic PDE theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide an alternative approach for the study of the Gaussian estimates of the solution of a fully coupled FBSDE, which is based on the use the classical PDE theory.
we provide Gaussian upper and lower estimates for the law, and the law is Gaussian if and only if it is Gaussian in the forward direction.

we provide a simple proof of Gaussian estimates for the law (or density) of the solution to an FBSDE, which is a key step in the study of the well-posedness of such equations, and also in their applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Gaussian density estimates for FBSDEs follow from the corresponding results for PDEs, without much additional work.
the Gaussian estimates for solutions to FBSDEs are essentially the same as the Gaussian estimates for the solutions to the associated parabolic PDE.
the Gaussian density estimates we obtain can be used to prove convergence rates in various settings.
